summary: Rabbi Harari explores the Gemara in Masekhet Bava Batra regarding the rights of neighbors in shared living spaces, specifically focusing on the responsibilities for building walls and the rights to light and space. He discusses the legal concept of a lien or usage right that a dweller may have over the space below or above them, and how these rights impact the ability of one neighbor to force changes or renovations on the other. The class examines the limits of these rights, including when a space becomes unusable or when specific conditions were stipulated at the time of purchase.
questions: Does a neighbor have the right to force me to contribute to the cost of a wall?
Can I force my neighbor to dismantle and rebuild our shared home if my living space has become uncomfortable?
What is the minimum height requirement for a living space before a neighbor can claim it is unusable?
Does a neighbor have the right to block my windows if I am willing to build new ones elsewhere?
Do I have rights to sunlight if the room being blocked is only used for storage?
